title: DECIMAL Data Type
description: Learn how to use the DECIMAL data type to store exact numeric values with fixed precision and scale.

data.text: The DECIMAL data type stores exact numeric values with fixed precision and scale. Use DECIMAL for monetary values or any data requiring exact arithmetic.

data.title: DECIMAL Syntax
data.content: Defines a DECIMAL column with precision and scale.

data.text: p is the precision (maximum total decimal digits, 1-38, default 38). s is the scale (decimal digits to the right of the decimal point, 0 to p). DECIMAL and NUMERIC are synonyms.

data.title: Create DECIMAL Column
data.content: Creates a table with DECIMAL and NUMERIC columns.

data.title: Insert DECIMAL Values
data.content: Inserts valid and invalid DECIMAL values.

data.text: The second insert fails with an arithmetic overflow error because the values exceed the precision and scale.

`DECIMAL(p, s)` has p total digits with s digits after the decimal point. Arithmetic widens the result using documented rules, so a division can return many more decimals than either operand had. Cast or `ROUND` when the result is presented as money.

data.title: Decimal precision in arithmetic
data.content: The rounded cast keeps exactly two decimals, which is what you want on a report.

data.title: The trap
data.text: Never compare `DECIMAL` values for equality in a `WHERE` clause unless the scale is guaranteed — normalise first. Also remember that `DECIMAL(38, 38)` cannot store a number greater than 1, because every digit sits after the decimal point.

data.title: DECIMAL Key Points
points: DECIMAL stores exact numeric values with fixed precision and scale.
Scale ranges from 0 to the precision value.
Storage size depends on the precision (5 to 17 bytes).
Use DECIMAL for monetary or exact arithmetic values.
